chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a man sends his dog (to hunt) and forgets to say 'Bismillah', he is in the same status as the one who slaughters (an animal) and forgets to say 'Bismillah', and similarly, when he throws an arrow and forgets to say 'Bismillah'.

key_terms.يُسَمِّيَ: To say the name of God (Bismillah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on hunting if one forgets to say Bismillah?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) draws a precise legal analogy between hunting and slaughter, ruling that forgetting to recite *Bismillah* renders the prey halal but distinct from those hunted with the invocation. This reflects the Shia juristic view that while the omission does not invalidate the meat, it affects the ritual completeness of the act, mirroring the status of *dhabihah* where the name was forgotten. The comparison underscores the importance of intentionality and verbal invocation in transforming natural acts into acts of worship.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the man sends his dog (to hunt) and forgets to Name (Bismillah), so he is at the status of the one slaughters and forgets to Name (Bismillah), and similar to that is when he throws with the spear and forgets to Name (Bismillah)’.
en.sarwar: 17. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Mu‘awiyah ibn Hakim from abu Malik al-Hadramiy from Jamil ibn Darraj who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about my sending a dog to hunt and after mentioning the name of Allah, when I have nothing with me to slaughter the prey.
He (the Imam) said, ‘Allow the dog to kill the prey, then you can use it for food.’”
